resources.string: Guards lock down the capabilities that malware needs (sending SMS, making calls, reading the screen, seeing what you type, accessing contacts, the microphone…), whatever way it arrived. All are off by default; enable them one by one, after the preview. They never act on system apps and services, on Watchpost or on its companion; the SMS guard spares the default SMS app, the Calls guard the default dialer. An app that gets itself chosen for one of those two roles (a system dialog, a single tap) is therefore not blocked by the matching guard: Watchpost flags it with a high-priority notification, read it. A keyboard or a home screen is spared by no guard. Denying a permission to an app also freezes, in Settings, the other permissions of the same group (they stay in their current state). An accessibility service that is already enabled can tap on your behalf, including inside Watchpost. "Restore everything" and the ADB rescue undo the guards.
Suggested order for a first try: Quarantine, Keyboards, Accessibility, Calls, SMS, and only then the "also…" options.
Denies sending SMS (SEND_SMS) to every app that asks for it, except the list below; also applies to apps installed or updated afterwards. A permission already granted is withdrawn.

Sending SMS from a third-party app (a messenger that also sends SMS, backup, home automation, an app that verifies your number, the carrier\'s visual voicemail, a watch or car app that replies by SMS): put the ones you need in the list. The "SMS" group of each denied app is frozen in Settings. With the option: automatic reading of codes received by SMS in third-party apps.

Does not block, only flags: the default SMS app. An app that gets itself designated default SMS app (one dialog, one tap: the usual route of SMS trojans) can send SMS; Watchpost grants it the role\'s permissions, adds it to the list and warns you with a high-priority notification — if it was not you, put your SMS app back and remove it from the list. Cannot prevent: sending by a system app; an SMS prepared by an app and sent by the SMS app (you must tap Send, unless an accessibility service does it: see the Accessibility guard); the few seconds between an install and the denial (up to 15 min if Watchpost was not running); what was sent before activation. A keyboard or a home screen is not spared. Watchpost does not count the SMS sent: without the experimental "Sensitive operations usage" collector (app_ops, off by default, ADB permissions), a mass send by an allowed app, or by the default SMS app, is visible nowhere.
Also deny reading and receiving SMS
READ_SMS, RECEIVE_SMS, RECEIVE_MMS, RECEIVE_WAP_PUSH: also prevents theft of codes received by SMS.
Denies placing calls (CALL_PHONE) to every app that asks for it, except the list; also to apps installed afterwards.

Direct calling from a third-party app (address book, home automation, watch, car, a taxi app that calls without going through the dialer). Opening the dialer with a prefilled number remains possible. The "Phone" group of each denied app is frozen in Settings: it can no longer obtain the phone state if it did not already have it (number verification in some messengers). A permission already granted is withdrawn, which stops the app on the spot. With the option: answering by a third-party app (watch, car through an app), call log in a third-party app.

Does not block, only flags: the default dialer (an app that gets itself chosen as dialer receives the role\'s permissions, enters the list, and a high-priority notification tells you). Cannot prevent: a call by a system app; a call prepared in the dialer and then confirmed (by you, or by an accessibility service); an Internet call (VoIP), which does not need this permission. A keyboard or a home screen is not spared. Calls placed are not counted without the experimental app_ops collector.
Also deny answering calls and the call log
Only approved accessibility services, and the system ones, can be enabled. This is the entry point of banking trojans: an accessibility service reads the screen and taps on your behalf.
Enabling a new password manager, an automation app (Tasker, MacroDroid), a blocker or a launcher that uses accessibility, if it is not in the list (Settings shows "disabled by the administrator").

Cannot prevent: a service that is already enabled (Android requires keeping it in the list: disable it in Settings first, then apply again) — and such a service can do anything on your behalf, including switching this guard off; a service from a system app; an app in the list that gets compromised. Android enforces this list in the Settings screen (the switch is greyed out), not in the service itself: not verified on One UI. If you depend on a service (screen reader, password manager), put it in the list yourself: a service that is only "kept" cannot be re-enabled after a re-application if it was disabled in the meantime.
Only approved keyboards, and the system ones (Samsung keyboard), can be enabled. A keyboard sees everything you type, passwords included.
Enabling a new keyboard (Gboard, SwiftKey…) without having added it to the list.

Cannot prevent: a keyboard that is already enabled (kept, Android requires it); a system keyboard; what an approved keyboard sees. Android enforces this list in the Settings screen only (the switch of a non-approved keyboard is greyed out): a keyboard that is already enabled keeps working, and the Samsung keyboard always remains available, including for the unlock code after a reboot.

Every non-system app installed after activation is denied SMS, calls, call log, contacts, microphone, camera, background location and nearby devices, until you release it. A notification tells you each time. Apps already present are not touched; an update of a released app does not put it back in quarantine.

An app you just installed cannot use these functions (video calls: microphone and camera; messenger: contacts; watch, earbuds, car, lock: Bluetooth and nearby devices — pairing fails without a message) before it is released. Its requests are denied without a dialog: Watchpost\'s notification is what tells you.

Cannot prevent: whatever needs no permission (Internet, overlay, accessibility, notifications: see the other guards); an app from the system or updated by the manufacturer\'s store; the few seconds after the install (up to 15 min if Watchpost was not running); an app installed in another space (Secure Folder, second user). A quarantined app chosen as default SMS app or dialer (one dialog, one tap) only receives the permissions of that role (otherwise incoming SMS and calls would be lost) and stays in quarantine for the rest (contacts, microphone, camera, location, nearby devices); a high-priority notification tells you. A keyboard or a home screen stays in quarantine.
App interrupted: it will be finished on the next pass (or "Disable")
List or option changed from the app: "Preview and re-apply" to put it into effect.
%1$d item(s) of this guard remain to be restored.
No installed app loses anything right now.

These apps were installed after the quarantine was enabled. The permissions listed are denied to them. "Release" puts them back in their state from before the quarantine: "ask" for an app that was just installed (it will ask you for them).
No risky permission requested for now (an update that requested one would be denied).
Release "%1$s"? It will be able to ask you again for: %2$s.
The Quarantine guard is off: enable it in Policy › Guards.
Guards: SMS app or dialer changed
An app was just designated default SMS app or dialer: this is the usual route of SMS trojans. High-priority notification.
Quarantine of a new app, change of default SMS app or dialer.
%1$s: %2$s denied until you release it in Watchpost.
%1$s: no risky permission requested for now; it stays monitored until you release it.
%1$s is now %2$s: added to the list of the "%3$s" guard%4$s. If it was not you, put your app back in Settings › Apps › Default apps, then remove it from the list in Watchpost.
, denials lifted and role permissions granted (%1$s)

%1$s is now %2$s while it is in quarantine: it receives the permissions of that role (%4$s) and stays in quarantine for the rest ("%3$s" guard). This is the usual route of SMS trojans: if it was not you, put your app back in Settings › Apps › Default apps; otherwise release it when you trust it.
